title: The Pharaoh's Names
objective: After this level you can explain the royal names and the cartouche.
summary: A pharaoh had five names, four of them given at coronation. The throne name and birth name were written inside a cartouche, a rope loop standing for eternity.

cards.headline: A pharaoh didn’t have a name. He had five.
cards.body: One came at birth; the other four arrived with the crown. Two of them were drawn inside a loop of rope. And one of them became the title of a famous English poem.

cards.headline: Five names, five titles
cards.body: A pharaoh’s full title had five names, each introduced by a title: Horus, Two Ladies, Golden Horus, King of Upper and Lower Egypt, and Son of Re. Only one name was given at birth; the other four came at his coronation. “King of Upper and Lower Egypt” should ring a bell: Level 6 showed every king held it after unification. Becoming king meant getting a whole new name tag.

cards.headline: The rope loop
cards.body: Two of the names, the throne name and the birth name, were written inside an oval called a cartouche. It shows a loop of rope and stands for a shen ring, a circle symbolizing eternity, wrapped protectively around the king’s name. The word itself is French for a paper cartridge, which is what the ovals looked like. Eternity, mistaken for ammunition.
cards.callout: Cartouche = rope loop = eternity around a name

mascot.line: Spot an oval full of hieroglyphs, and you’ve found a royal name.

cards.headline: Names at work
cards.body: Names carried messages. Tutankhaten became Tutankhamun as Egypt went back to the old gods (Level 71). And Ramesses II’s throne name, Usermaatre, came out in Greek as “Ozymandias,” the king of Shelley’s poem (Level 72). The cartouche promised eternity; the pronunciation got lost in translation.

cards.headline: Royal names: read
learned: A pharaoh had five names, four given at coronation
The throne name and birth name went in cartouches
A cartouche is a rope loop standing for eternity
Usermaatre, Ramesses II’s throne name, became “Ozymandias”

questions.prompt: How many names made up a pharaoh’s full royal title?

options.label: Two
options.rationale: Two of them went in cartouches; there were more.

questions.explanation: Horus, Two Ladies, Golden Horus, King of Upper and Lower Egypt and Son of Re each introduced one of five names.

questions.prompt: What did the oval cartouche around a king’s name stand for?

options.label: A gun cartridge, which Egyptians invented
options.rationale: The cartridge idea came from much later French speakers.

options.label: The shape of the king’s tomb
options.rationale: It showed a rope loop, not a tomb.

options.label: A shen ring, a symbol of eternity protecting the name
The Nile’s yearly flood
options.rationale: It was about eternity and protection.

questions.explanation: The cartouche is a rope loop representing a shen ring, a circle symbolizing eternity that protects the name inside.

questions.prompt: A pharaoh’s titles included “King of Upper and Lower Egypt”; from Level 6, where was Upper Egypt?

options.label: The northern Delta, by the sea
The red desert beyond the valley
options.rationale: Both lands were named by the Nile.

options.label: Along the Red Sea coast
options.rationale: Both lands lay along the river.

questions.explanation: Upper Egypt was upstream, the long valley in the south; Lower Egypt was the northern Delta.
